mandatory_explanations.text: The complete selected Ethiopic unit is printed before XXXIII. It has a singular aged father and a singular mother, followed by the plural ancestral expression አበዋቲከ፡ እለ፡ ቀደሙከ. “Your ancestors who preceded you” is a bounded, explicitly provisional apposition to those two people, not a replacement by Adam and Eve or an invented additional group. The actual longer ancestral word corrects an earlier shortened draft transcription; the primary father entry permits plural parents and forebears. The selected plural opened-eyes, knowing, nakedness and expulsion clauses remain Ethiopic text, without a supplied agent. The facing Greek gives only the short father/eating clause followed by editorial dots; it does not attest the entire Ethiopic unit, and its dots do not mark a missing Ethiopic ending. Dillmann1851 was used only as an aligned edited-Geʽez comparison, not to replace Charles’s selected word order or claim fresh manuscripts.
